newsitem.title: GERMANY: TV ads boosted ProSieben bourse launch.
newsitem.headline: TV ads boosted ProSieben bourse launch.

text.p: Television company ProSieben AG chairman Georg Kofler pointed to the success of its TV advertising campaign as paving the way to a high-profile public listing on Monday.

Kofler said the TV ad campaign for its bourse launch had been second in size in German history only to Deutsche Telekom's share debut promotion last fall and credited it with giving Monday's start top billing.
"With this campaign, we set a new standard not only in terms of volume and media planning, but also for advertising quality and effectiveness," Kofler said.

Kofler said polls prior to the float showed that 75 percent of people who had heard about the initial public offering knew about it from TV, and that its information phone number, which was provided in the ads, had tallied 800,000 callers.

He declined to say how much the company had spent on the television campaign, saying comparisons would be inaccurate because the company had produced the ads in-house and broadcast them mainly on their own TV channels.
Pro Sieben AG shares traded well above their initial public offering price of 72 marks after their introduction on Monday, closing at 95 marks in Frankfurt bourse trade.
